subject: Cloud Computing
title: Power and Cooling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Power and Cooling.

hook.text: A large data center consumes as much electricity as a small city — up to 100 megawatts.

buildup.text: Every watt of computing produces heat. Without cooling, servers would overheat in minutes.

discovery.text: PUE measures efficiency: how much total power versus computing power. Ideal is 1.0, most hit 1.2.

twist.text: Some data centers use river water, ocean air, or even arctic locations for free natural cooling.

climax.text: Microsoft sank a data center underwater. It ran for two years with fewer failures than on land.

punchline.text: Cloud computing's biggest enemy isn't hackers. It's heat.

quiz.question: What does PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) measure?
options: How efficiently a data center converts total power into computing power
The maximum number of users a data center can support
How quickly power can be restored after an outage

details.summary: Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity, with most energy going to servers and cooling. Modern facilities use innovative cooling techniques like free air cooling, liquid cooling, and strategic placement in cold climates to improve efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
details.whyItMatters: Power and cooling are the biggest operational costs and environmental concerns for cloud providers. Efficiency improvements directly reduce the carbon footprint of every cloud workload.
takeaways: Cooling can account for 30-40% of data center energy use
PUE measures how efficiently power is used for computing
Free air and liquid cooling dramatically improve efficiency

faq.question: What is PUE in practice?
faq.answer: Power Usage Effectiveness measures data center efficiency as total facility power divided by IT equipment power. A PUE of 1.0 means all power goes to computing. Modern cloud data centers achieve PUE of 1.1 to 1.2, compared to 2.0 or higher for older facilities.

faq.question: How do cloud providers cool their data centers?
faq.answer: Methods include traditional air conditioning, hot/cold aisle containment, free air cooling using outside air in cool climates, evaporative cooling, and liquid cooling where coolant flows directly to server components. Google uses AI to optimize cooling controls in real time.
